sections.title: 1. System access and responsibilities
steps: Open the PK Document Control address supplied by your system administrator in your browser.
Obtain your own Username and password from the administrator. Account creation and password resets are managed in User Management.
Use Hardcopy Documents to find physical records and their storage location or holder. Use Softcopy Documents to find controlled electronic records and their current files.
Use My Requests when you need approval to create, change, transfer, dispose of, access, or be assigned a document.
Use My Tasks to review approval work assigned to your account or one of your roles, and to complete physical transfer handoffs.
Authorized document controllers and administrators also receive management menus for direct actions, assignments, reference places, users, roles, workflows, audit, and backups.
notes: Menus, records, request actions, and file buttons depend on your permissions and document access. A colleague may see different options.
This guide describes the existing PK Document Control interface. Ask your administrator when a needed menu or document is unavailable; do not use another person's account.
Document access does not automatically grant permission to edit, download, print, approve, or administer the system.
slide_steps: Open the address supplied by your system administrator and use your own account.
Hardcopy Documents tracks physical records; Softcopy Documents provides controlled electronic records and files.
Use My Requests for approval proposals and My Tasks for assigned approvals or physical handoffs.
Document controllers and administrators receive extra management menus when permitted.
Ask the administrator when a needed menu, action, or record is unavailable.
slide_notes: Menus, records, request actions, and file buttons depend on your permissions and document access. A colleague may see different options.

sections.title: 2. Sign in and change your password
steps: On Sign in to your account, enter your Username and Password, then select Sign In.
If Change your temporary password appears, enter the Current or temporary password, a New password, and Confirm new password.
Choose a new password with more than 8 characters, up to 72 bytes, and do not reuse the temporary password. Enter the same new password in both new-password fields.
Select Set permanent password. You must finish this setup before accessing documents, requests, or administration.
To change your password later, open your name at the top right and select Change Password. Complete the three password fields, then select Update Password and confirm the action.
To leave the system, open the same account menu, select Sign Out, and confirm.
notes: If Invalid username or password appears, recheck the credentials. After too many failed attempts, wait before trying again or contact the administrator.
There is no self-service password recovery form on the sign-in screen. An administrator can generate a new temporary password.
Your name and role appear in the account menu. The available self-service account action is Change Password.
slide_steps: Enter Username and Password, then select Sign In.
For a temporary password, complete Current or temporary password, New password, and Confirm new password.
Choose more than 8 characters, up to 72 bytes; select Set permanent password.
Later, open your name → Change Password, complete the fields, then Update Password → Confirm.
Open your name → Sign Out → Confirm to finish your session.
slide_notes: If Invalid username or password appears, recheck the credentials. After too many failed attempts, wait before trying again or contact the administrator.

sections.title: 3. Overview and main navigation
steps: Select Overview in the left navigation to return to your dashboard.
Read Accessible documents for the number of records you are authorized to see, and Created by you for records you created within that access.
Read Pending approvals for work assigned to you or your role, and Outstanding handoffs for your physical dispatch or receipt tasks.
Use Your document register to compare accessible Hardcopy and Softcopy counts. Use My request status to see the status distribution of your own requests.
Open Hardcopy Documents or Softcopy Documents under Document Management to browse records.
Open My Requests or My Tasks under Document Requests. Their badges indicate draft or returned requests and pending tasks respectively.
On a narrow screen, use the Toggle navigation menu button to show the navigation. Open your name at the top right for account actions, and use the bell to open Notifications.
notes: Dashboard numbers reflect your authorized records and work, rather than an unrestricted company-wide total.
Additional menus appear only when your account has the corresponding permissions.
slide_steps: Select Overview for your dashboard. On narrow screens, use Toggle navigation to show the sidebar.
Check Accessible documents and Created by you for counts within your document access.
Check Pending approvals and Outstanding handoffs for work assigned to you or your roles.
Read Your document register and My request status to see document and request distributions.
Use the left navigation for documents, My Requests, My Tasks, and permitted management pages; use the bell for Notifications.
slide_notes: Dashboard numbers reflect your authorized records and work, rather than an unrestricted company-wide total.

sections.title: 4. Find and inspect document records
steps: Open Hardcopy Documents or Softcopy Documents, then choose Table or Folder in the Document Browser.
In Table view, enter text in Search records. Narrow the results with All Statuses, All Owners, and the date-period control when needed.
For dates, choose All time, Today, This week, This month, This year, or Custom range. Custom range provides Start date and End date. Select Clear to remove filters.
In Folder view, open folders to follow the hierarchy. Hardcopy folders follow Area, Specific, optional Asset, and Location; softcopy folders follow categories and subcategories.
Use the folder breadcrumbs to return to a parent. Use Recent, A–Z, or Z–A to change document ordering, and All Documents when you need the full authorized register.
Select the document title or View action to open its details. Hardcopy records show storage, custody, retention, related requests, approval history, and transfer history where recorded.
For softcopy details, inspect Revision & Classification, Document Files, Related Requests, and Approval History. Select Close when finished.
Use Rows per page and the previous or next page controls for longer lists.
notes: Hardcopy table columns include Document Title, Location, Holder, and Status. Softcopy columns include Document Title, Document Number, Category, and Status.
Only authorized folders and records are available. Status filters include Active, Disposed, and Cancelled.
slide_steps: Open Hardcopy Documents or Softcopy Documents and choose Table or Folder.
Use Search records, status, owner, and date filters. Select Clear to remove filters.
Expand hardcopy Area → Specific → optional Asset → Location, or softcopy category folders. Use breadcrumbs and All Documents to change scope.
Open a document title or View action for full details, related requests, approval history, and applicable file or transfer history.
Use Rows per page, page arrows, and Recent / A–Z / Z–A ordering to browse long lists.
slide_notes: Hardcopy table columns include Document Title, Location, Holder, and Status. Softcopy columns include Document Title, Document Number, Category, and Status.

sections.title: 5. Request a hardcopy record or update
steps: Open My Requests, select Hardcopy Requests, and select New Request.
Choose Create or Update in Request Action and enter Subject / Reason. For Update, first choose the Existing Hardcopy Document.
Enter the Document Title and select its Area, Specific, optional Asset, and Location. Choose entries from the system lists so the storage hierarchy remains consistent.
Check Current Holder. For an ordinary requester it uses the signed-in account; an administrator may select a holder.
Optionally enable Track retention period. When enabled, enter both Retention Start and Retention End; End must be on or after Start.
Add optional Reason / Notes or remarks where displayed. Check the proposed storage and holder before saving.
Select Save Draft and confirm. Back in the list, open View to check the proposal, then select Submit and confirm to start approval.
Follow the request in My Requests. The proposed record or update is applied after the required approvals complete.
notes: Asset is optional; Area, Specific, and Location are required in the hardcopy form.
A saved draft has not yet entered approval. Use Submit after checking it.
Use Hardcopy Transfer for a physical handoff rather than treating a draft metadata update as proof of receipt.
slide_steps: Open My Requests → Hardcopy Requests → New Request; choose Create or Update and enter Subject / Reason.
For Update, select Existing Hardcopy Document. Enter or check Document Title and the storage hierarchy.
Choose Area, Specific, optional Asset, and Location; check Current Holder.
Optionally enable retention monitoring and enter both Start and End dates (End on/after Start). Add notes, then Save Draft and Confirm.
Review the saved proposal, then Submit → Confirm. Track its approval before treating the proposed change as applied.
slide_notes: Asset is optional; Area, Specific, and Location are required in the hardcopy form.

sections.title: 6. Request a new softcopy document
steps: Open My Requests, select Softcopy Requests, and select New Request.
Set Softcopy Action to Create Softcopy and enter Subject / Reason.
Enter Proposed Document Title and Document Number, add the optional Series Number if used, and choose the Category.
Under Document File, choose the file that approvers must review. Supported choices shown by the form are PDF, TXT, PNG, JPG, JPEG, DOCX, and XLSX, with a 15 MB maximum.
Add optional Remarks to explain the proposal or direct approvers to a point that needs attention.
Select Save Draft and confirm. Open the saved request to check its title, classification, and attachment; use Review File when available.
Select Submit and confirm to send the draft through the published approval workflow.
Check My Requests for progress. Once approved and completed, find the controlled record in Softcopy Documents.
notes: Create and Revise require a document file. When editing an existing draft, the already attached file can be retained unless you select a replacement.
Fields appear according to the selected action. Creation does not show every revision-specific field.
An attachment in a draft or submitted request is a proposal until the workflow completes.
slide_steps: Open My Requests → Softcopy Requests → New Request and choose Create Softcopy.
Enter Subject / Reason, Proposed Document Title, Document Number, optional Series Number, and Category.
Attach the Document File: PDF, TXT, PNG, JPG, JPEG, DOCX, or XLSX; maximum 15 MB.
Add optional Remarks, then Save Draft → Confirm. Review the saved proposal and attachment.
Select Submit → Confirm and track the approval. The completed record appears in Softcopy Documents.
slide_notes: Create and Revise require a document file. When editing an existing draft, the already attached file can be retained unless you select a replacement.

sections.title: 7. Revise, cancel, download, or print softcopies
steps: To propose a revision, open My Requests → Softcopy Requests → New Request and choose Revise Softcopy.
Choose Existing Softcopy Document. Check the loaded document information, enter Subject / Reason, and confirm the Proposed Document Title.
Enter New Revision Level and Number of Pages, choose an optional Effective Date, and attach the revised Document File. A blank Effective Date defaults to approval day.
Add Remarks, select Save Draft and confirm, review the proposal, then Submit it for approval.
To request cancellation of an existing controlled record, choose Cancel Softcopy, select the document, explain Subject / Reason, and save and submit the request.
To obtain the current authorized file, open Softcopy Documents and use Download or Print on the record when those buttons are available.
For a printable preview, wait for preparation, then select Print. For an Office file without a browser print preview, download it and use File → Print in Word or Excel.
Use Document File History to inspect available revision entries when permitted. Check the Current or Superseded label before using a file.
notes: Download and Print links in file history are offered for current files, subject to your file permissions. Historical entries do not imply the old file remains downloadable.
Cancel Softcopy is a controlled-document action; Cancel on a draft request cancels that draft.
slide_steps: For revision, choose Revise Softcopy and select Existing Softcopy Document.
Check the title, enter New Revision Level and Number of Pages, and attach the revised file. Effective Date is optional.
Save Draft → Confirm, review the proposal, then Submit → Confirm.
For controlled cancellation, choose Cancel Softcopy, select the document, and explain Subject / Reason before saving and submitting.
Use permitted Download, Print, and Document File History actions in Softcopy Documents for the current controlled file.
slide_notes: Download and Print links in file history are offered for current files, subject to your file permissions. Historical entries do not imply the old file remains downloadable.

sections.title: 8. Save, submit, and track requests
steps: Open My Requests and choose the tab for the work: Softcopy Requests, Hardcopy Requests, Hardcopy Transfer, Hardcopy Disposal, Document Access Grants, or Document Assignments.
Select New Request, choose an available Request Action, and complete the fields that appear for that action.
Select Save Draft and approve the confirmation. A Draft remains editable by its requester when the necessary permissions are present.
Open View to check Request & Ownership, the proposed metadata, the Document File where relevant, and the Approval Process Timeline.
Select Submit and confirm when ready. Submitted indicates that the request is awaiting its workflow; use the timeline and Workflow Activity Log to identify the current stage and recorded decisions.
If the request is Returned to you, read the recorded remarks, edit the proposal, save it, and Submit again.
Use Cancel on a Draft that you no longer need. If Delete becomes available on your cancelled, never-submitted draft, it permanently removes that draft after confirmation.
Search using Request Reference, and use status, action, or date filters to find older requests.
notes: Statuses shown by the request filter are Draft, Submitted, Completed, Approved, Rejected, Returned, and Cancelled. Approved transfers still need the physical handoff steps.
Only the requester may edit their own draft or returned request. Submitted requests are not editable drafts.
A published workflow must be available. Resubmitting a returned request keeps its original workflow version.
slide_steps: Choose the appropriate My Requests tab and select New Request; complete the action-specific fields.
Save Draft → Confirm records the proposal. Open View to inspect metadata, any attachment, and its approval timeline.
Select Submit → Confirm when ready. Submitted means the published approval workflow has started.
For a request Returned to you, read the remarks, Edit, save, and Submit again.
Cancel an unwanted Draft. Delete is permanent and is offered only for your cancelled, never-submitted draft.
slide_notes: Statuses shown by the request filter are Draft, Submitted, Completed, Approved, Rejected, Returned, and Cancelled. Approved transfers still need the physical handoff steps.

sections.title: 9. Request document access or assignment
steps: Open My Requests and choose Document Access Grants to request access, or Document Assignments to request that a document be assigned to you.
Select New Request. Check the Request Action, then enter the Subject explaining what you need.
Choose Document Type: Softcopy or Hardcopy. Select the corresponding Softcopy Document or Hardcopy Document from the list.
Check Recipient / Assigned User. In these request tabs the recipient is your signed-in account and is read-only.
For a Grant Access request, set Access Expires At. Add optional Remarks that help the approvers understand the purpose.
Select Save Draft and confirm. Inspect the saved request, then select Submit and confirm.
Follow the Approval Process Timeline and Workflow Activity Log in View. When completed, return to the appropriate document register and check the access or assignment.
notes: Request access and Request assignment are approval requests for yourself. Authorized controllers assign records to other users through Document Assignments in the Document Control menu.
Only the document field matching the selected Document Type is active.
An access grant does not itself enable file actions your role is not permitted to use.
slide_steps: Open My Requests → Document Access Grants or Document Assignments and select New Request.
Enter Subject, choose Document Type, and select the Softcopy or Hardcopy Document.
Check Recipient / Assigned User: it is your signed-in account and is read-only.
For access, set Access Expires At; add optional Remarks. Save Draft → Confirm, then Submit → Confirm.
Inspect the Approval Process Timeline and verify the completed access or assignment in the document register.
slide_notes: Request access and Request assignment are approval requests for yourself. Authorized controllers assign records to other users through Document Assignments in the Document Control menu.

sections.title: 10. Request a hardcopy transfer
steps: Open My Requests → Hardcopy Transfer and select New Request.
Select the Hardcopy Document you intend to transfer. Read Original Places and Holder, which loads the document title, current storage hierarchy, location sequence, and current holder.
Under Transfer Destination, select Destination Area, Destination Specific, optional Destination Asset, and Destination Location.
Check the completed hierarchy. Selecting a child can fill its parents; the destination location must differ from the original location.
Choose Receiving User and enter Request Subject. Add optional Remarks to explain the move.
Select Save Draft and confirm, review the original and destination information, then select Submit and confirm.
Track approval in My Requests. After approval, use My Tasks → Hardcopy Transfer to record Dispatch and Accept at the actual handoff stages.
notes: The available hardcopy list is limited to records the system permits you to transfer.
Approval authorizes the transfer; the physical handoff is completed separately.
A transfer needs a receiving user and a destination; a remark alone does not update custody.
slide_steps: Open My Requests → Hardcopy Transfer → New Request and select Hardcopy Document.
Check Original Places and Holder, including location sequence.
Choose the destination Area, Specific, optional Asset, and Location. Destination must differ from the original.
Select Receiving User, enter Request Subject, and add optional Remarks; Save Draft → Confirm, then Submit → Confirm.
After approval, complete dispatch and recipient acceptance in My Tasks → Hardcopy Transfer.
slide_notes: The available hardcopy list is limited to records the system permits you to transfer.

sections.title: 11. Dispatch and accept the physical hardcopy
steps: Open My Tasks and select Hardcopy Transfer after the transfer has been approved.
Find the Physical Transfer Handoffs section below the request list. Check Hardcopy, Requester / Dispatcher, Current Holder, Recipient, and Stage.
As the transfer requester, locate the approved handoff awaiting transfer. Select Dispatch when physically releasing the correct document to the intended recipient.
Check the Dispatch Hardcopy confirmation and select Confirm. The system records the release and awaits recipient acceptance.
As the destination recipient, open My Tasks → Hardcopy Transfer and locate the handoff marked In Transit.
After receiving and checking the physical document, select Accept and then Confirm.
Reopen Hardcopy Documents and inspect the holder and location to verify the completed receipt. Use Transfer History in the document details when checking the recorded handoff.
notes: Only the transfer requester can dispatch. Only the destination recipient can accept.
Accept confirms physical receipt and updates custody and location. Record these actions when the physical handoff actually occurs.
Users may receive dispatch or receipt tasks even when they are not general workflow approvers.
slide_steps: Open My Tasks → Hardcopy Transfer and find Physical Transfer Handoffs.
Check the document, requester, current holder, recipient, and stage.
The requester selects Dispatch at physical release, then Confirm.
After physical receipt, the recipient selects Accept for the In Transit handoff, then Confirm.
Inspect the updated holder, location, and Transfer History in Hardcopy Documents.
slide_notes: Only the transfer requester can dispatch. Only the destination recipient can accept.

sections.title: 12. Request hardcopy disposal
steps: Open My Requests → Hardcopy Disposal and select New Request.
Check Request Action and enter Subject / Reason explaining the disposal proposal.
Choose the Hardcopy Document. Recheck its title, holder, location, and retention information in the register before proceeding.
Select Disposal Reason: Shred, Scratch, or Other. If you choose Other, complete Other Reason.
Add optional Remarks, select Save Draft, and confirm.
Review the saved proposal, then select Submit and confirm to send it for approval.
Follow the request status and recorded decisions. After completion, open the hardcopy record using the Disposed status filter and inspect Disposal Details.
notes: Saving the disposal proposal does not complete the approval process.
Only authorized users receive direct Dispose actions in the document register. That direct action also requires a disposal reason and confirmation.
Track retention period provides record information; follow your organization's disposal procedure when carrying out the physical disposal.
slide_steps: Open My Requests → Hardcopy Disposal → New Request.
Enter Subject / Reason and select Hardcopy Document; check its location, holder, and retention details.
Choose Shred, Scratch, or Other; complete Other Reason when selected. Add optional Remarks.
Save Draft → Confirm, review the proposal, then Submit → Confirm.
After approval completes, use the Disposed filter to inspect Disposal Details in the register.
slide_notes: Saving the disposal proposal does not complete the approval process.

sections.title: 13. Review and decide approval tasks
steps: Open My Tasks and choose the request category. Use the tab badge, Search records, or the Request Reference to find the item awaiting your review.
Open View. Read Request & Ownership, the proposed document information, the Approval Process Timeline, and Workflow Activity Log.
For a softcopy request with an attachment, use Review File to inspect the proposed file before deciding.

For an Office attachment, use Open in Word or Excel, Open in WPS, or Download as offered. If WPS opening requires setup, use Download WPS opener setup and follow its README, or download and open the file normally.
Choose Approve when the proposal should move forward, Reject when it should stop, or Return when the preceding stage needs to review it again.
For Approve, read the shared confirmation and select Confirm. For Return or Reject, enter an optional Remark and select Continue; Continue itself confirms that decision.
Reopen the request details to verify the recorded decision and the next stage. The final approval applies the document action; approved transfers continue to dispatch and receipt.
notes: Only the currently assigned approver, or an authorized member of the assigned role, may decide.

Return at the first approval step sends the request to its requester for correction. Return at a later step reactivates the immediately previous approver; it does not always send the request to the requester.
Review File opens the proposal for inspection; use the task's decision buttons to record approval.
slide_steps: Open My Tasks, choose a category, and open the assigned request's View details.
Read the proposal, Approval Process Timeline, and Workflow Activity Log; use Review File for an attached softcopy.
Choose Approve → Confirm to move the current step forward.
Choose Return or Reject, enter an optional Remark, then Continue to record the decision.
Inspect the updated timeline. Return at step one sends to the requester; later-step Return reactivates the previous approver.
slide_notes: Only the currently assigned approver, or an authorized member of the assigned role, may decide.

sections.title: 14. Read notifications and approval reminders
steps: Select the bell at the top of the workspace to open Notifications. Its badge represents unread notifications.
Read the Request Reference, document or task title, and approval label for each entry.
Select an entry to mark that notification read and open the corresponding My Tasks category filtered to the request reference.
Use Previous, Next, and Rows in the notification panel when there are multiple pages.
If an Approval needed reminder appears, read the new-task list, open the relevant task link when needed, or select Got it to close the reminder.
Use My Tasks to perform the actual review and decision. Use My Tasks → Hardcopy Transfer for physical dispatch or acceptance work.
notes: Opening the notification panel alone does not mark every item read; selecting an entry acknowledges that notification.
Reading or dismissing a notification does not approve or reject its request.
No unread notifications means the inbox has no unread entries; continue to use My Tasks to check current assigned work.
slide_steps: Open the bell to read Notifications and their Request Reference, title, and approval label.
Select an entry to mark that notification read and open the matching My Tasks list.
Use Previous, Next, and Rows for additional notification pages.
If Approval needed appears, inspect its new-task links or select Got it.
Use My Tasks to record the actual decision or handoff; reading a notice does not approve it.
slide_notes: Opening the notification panel alone does not mark every item read; selecting an entry acknowledges that notification.

sections.title: 15. Apply authorized direct document actions
steps: Open the relevant document register. Direct-action buttons appear only to users who have the required direct permission.
To add a hardcopy directly, select Hardcopy Direct, enter Document Title, Area, Specific, optional Asset, Location, and Current Holder, and complete optional retention information or Reason / Notes.
Select Save Document, review the confirmation, and continue. Check the saved record in the register.
To create, revise, or cancel a softcopy directly, select Softcopy Direct and choose the Softcopy Action. Complete the same action-specific information used in a softcopy request.
Attach a Document File for direct Create or Revise. Select Approve Directly, check the confirmation, and continue to apply the action.
Use Edit on an active, manageable hardcopy to change its metadata. On softcopies, Edit opens a direct revision action.
If Dispose is available and appropriate, choose the disposal reason, complete Other Reason when required, and confirm. Inspect the resulting status and record details.
notes: Direct softcopy actions are approved and applied immediately by the authorized operator. Use My Requests when approval through the workflow is required.
Edit and Dispose require an active record within the operator's permitted scope. Dispose also requires direct disposal permission.
An ordinary user's hardcopy holder is fixed to that user's account; administrators can select a holder.
slide_steps: Open the permitted document register. Direct actions require the corresponding direct permission.
For a hardcopy, select Hardcopy Direct and complete title, storage hierarchy, holder, and optional retention or notes.
Select Save Document → Confirm, then inspect the saved record.
For a softcopy, choose Softcopy Direct, select the action, and complete the visible fields; Create and Revise require a file.
Select Approve Directly → Confirm. Edit an active record or use Dispose with a disposal reason only when those actions are permitted.
slide_notes: Direct softcopy actions are approved and applied immediately by the authorized operator. Use My Requests when approval through the workflow is required.

sections.title: 16. Assign documents directly to users
steps: Open Document Assignments under Document Control. Choose Hardcopy / Places or Softcopy / Categories.
For one document, select Assign Document, choose the Hardcopy Document or Softcopy Document, and choose Assigned User.
Select Save Assignment and confirm. Check the register's Document, Assigned To, and Updated values.
To change an existing assignment, use Edit on its row, choose the correct Assigned User, save, and confirm.
For all active hardcopies at a location, choose Location and Assigned User in the location assignment panel, then select Assign All and confirm.
For active softcopies in a category, choose Category / Subcategory and Assigned User, then select Assign All and confirm. The confirmation includes the category's subcategories.
Use Search records and All Assigned Users to inspect assignments. In User Management, the Assigned Documents action provides another view of a selected user's active assigned records.
notes: This page applies assignments directly and requires direct assignment permission. Approval-based assignment requests remain in My Requests → Document Assignments.
Read the selected location or category carefully before confirming Assign All, because it applies to multiple active records.
Physical transfer requests have their own approval, dispatch, and acceptance flow.
slide_steps: Open Document Assignments and choose Hardcopy / Places or Softcopy / Categories.
Select Assign Document, choose the document and Assigned User, then Save Assignment → Confirm.
Use Edit on an assignment to change its Assigned User; check Document, Assigned To, and Updated.
For a bulk hardcopy assignment, select Location and Assigned User, then Assign All → Confirm.
For softcopies, select Category / Subcategory and Assigned User, then Assign All → Confirm; subcategories are included.
slide_notes: This page applies assignments directly and requires direct assignment permission. Approval-based assignment requests remain in My Requests → Document Assignments.

sections.title: 17. Maintain places and softcopy categories
steps: Open Setup Places and choose the permitted tab: Area, Specific, Asset, Location, or Softcopy Categories.
Use the Add button for the selected tab to create reference data, or Edit to update an existing item.
Create an Area by name; create a Specific under its Area; create an Asset Number under its Specific. These relationships support hardcopy storage choices.
For a Location, enter Location Name and select Area and Specific. Asset Number is optional. Enter Sequence if a particular order is required, or leave it empty for automatic ordering.
Check the location sequence guidance: it is unique within the Specific, with A = 1, B = 2, and C = 3. Complete optional Archive Date where used.
For Softcopy Categories, complete Name, Folder, optional Description, and the Parent when making a subcategory.
Check the Active option, select Save Record, and confirm. Use status and parent filters to find saved items.
Use Deactivate when a reference item should no longer be active; historical links are preserved.
notes: Only tabs and actions permitted for the current account are shown.
A Location can be saved without an Asset Number. Keep Area and Specific consistent when choosing children.
Deactivating reference data is different from disposing of a document record.
slide_steps: Open Setup Places and choose Area, Specific, Asset, Location, or Softcopy Categories.
Use Add or Edit. Maintain Area → Specific → optional Asset before selecting Location.
For Location, enter Location Name, Area, Specific, optional Asset Number, and optional Sequence or Archive Date.
For Softcopy Categories, enter Name, Folder, optional Description, and Parent for a subcategory.
Check Active, then Save Record → Confirm. Deactivate an unused reference item to preserve its historical links.
slide_notes: Only tabs and actions permitted for the current account are shown.

sections.title: 18. Create and maintain user accounts
steps: Open User Management. Search the list or filter by status and role to find an account; use View to inspect its details.
Select Add User, or use Edit for an existing account. Enter First Name, optional Middle Name, Last Name, Username, and Position Title.
Choose Primary role and check the Assigned roles that the account should receive. Select Leader when required by the person's approval workflow.
Check Active account, select Save User, and confirm.
For a new user, read the Temporary account credentials page. Provide the generated Username and temporary password to that account owner through your approved private channel.
For an existing user who needs a password reset, edit the account and select Generate a new temporary password for this existing account, then save and confirm.
Use Deactivate to disable an eligible account while preserving its related history. Use Assigned Documents, when available, to inspect its active hardcopy and softcopy assignments.
notes: The generated temporary password is displayed once after saving. The user must replace it before accessing protected modules.
A Leader is optional in account data, but submission needs an active leader when the configured workflow uses Requester's leader.
Account actions have permission restrictions. The interface does not offer self-deactivation, and administrator accounts have additional protection.
slide_steps: Open User Management and select Add User or Edit an existing eligible account.
Complete First Name, optional Middle Name, Last Name, Username, and Position Title.
Choose Primary role and Assigned roles; select an optional Leader when the workflow needs one.
Check Active account, then Save User → Confirm. New-account credentials appear once; share privately with the owner.
Use Generate a new temporary password for a reset, Deactivate to disable an eligible account, or Assigned Documents to inspect assignments.
slide_notes: The generated temporary password is displayed once after saving. The user must replace it before accessing protected modules.

sections.title: 19. Maintain roles and permissions
steps: Open Roles & Permissions and use the search or All Statuses filter to find a role.
Select Add Role to create a role, or Edit to update an eligible existing role.
Enter Role Name and check Active role as appropriate.
Under Module Permissions, select the actions this role may use. Review the full list before saving so the role matches the person's responsibilities.
Select Save Role and confirm. Check the saved role and its status.
Assign the role to the intended accounts in User Management using Primary role and Assigned roles.
Use Deactivate for an unused role when the action is available. Permanently remove a role only when the interface offers removal for an unused role and the role is no longer required.
notes: Permissions control both visible menus and individual actions such as direct changes, requests, downloads, and printing.
A user's assigned document access and current workflow assignment still determine which records or tasks they can act on.
Deactivation and permanent removal are separate actions; read the confirmation before continuing.
slide_steps: Open Roles & Permissions; search or filter to find the role.
Select Add Role or Edit and enter Role Name; check Active role as appropriate.
Under Module Permissions, select only the actions needed for this role.
Select Save Role → Confirm, then assign the role to users in User Management.
Use Deactivate or permanent Remove only when offered for an unused role, and read the confirmation carefully.
slide_notes: Permissions control both visible menus and individual actions such as direct changes, requests, downloads, and printing.

sections.title: 20. Configure and publish approval workflows
steps: Open Workflow Builder and find the workflow for the relevant Request Type. Open its Steps action to inspect the approval route.
Use Workflow Version to inspect the available versions. Published versions are read-only.
Select Start First Draft or Create Next Draft when available to create an editable approval version.
Select Add Approval Step, enter Approval Step Name, and choose Approver Type: Any active member of role, Specific user, Requester's leader, or Requester account.
Choose Approver Role or Specific Approver when the selected type requires it, then select Save Step and confirm.
Use Edit, the up and down controls, and Remove to arrange the draft's approval steps. Check the full route in order, including its final approval.
Select Validate & Publish and confirm when the draft is ready to be the default for future requests.
Check that the intended published version is shown. Create another draft for later changes rather than editing the published version.
notes: A workflow supports up to 30 approval steps and needs an approval route before publication.
Requester and Requester's leader are resolved when the request is submitted. Ensure the relevant accounts, roles, and leaders are active.
Publishing changes future requests. Existing submitted requests, including returned requests that are resubmitted, retain their original approval timeline.
slide_steps: Open Workflow Builder, find the Request Type, and open Steps. Use Workflow Version to inspect the route.
Select Start First Draft or Create Next Draft; published versions are read-only.
Add Approval Step, enter its name, and select a role, specific user, Requester's leader, or Requester account; Save Step → Confirm.
Edit, move, or remove draft steps until the order is correct, then Validate & Publish → Confirm.
Check the published default. Future requests use it; existing submitted requests keep their original approval timeline.
slide_notes: A workflow supports up to 30 approval steps and needs an approval route before publication.

sections.title: 21. Inspect the Internal Audit Trail
steps: Open Internal Audit Trail under System Administration.
Use Search records to find the relevant person, action, or subject recorded in the audit list.
Choose All Results, Success, or Failed to narrow the outcome. Use the available date controls when investigating a time period.
Read Recorded At, User, Action, Subject, and Result to identify the event.
Open View for the row. The Audit Event details show Recorded Activity, including User ID and any recorded Details.
Select Close when finished and use the page controls to continue through the list.
For document-specific approval or handoff questions, also inspect Approval History, Related Requests, or Transfer History in the document details.
notes: The audit page is a read-only inspection screen; it does not provide an edit or delete operation for audit events.
If a warning is shown on the page, include it when reporting an investigation to the administrator.
The navigation provides this Internal Audit Trail and the Overview charts. No separate Reports menu or report-export control is present in these screens.
slide_steps: Open Internal Audit Trail and search for the relevant user, action, or subject.
Filter All Results, Success, or Failed and choose the required date period.
Read Recorded At, User, Action, Subject, and Result.
Open View for Audit Event details, including User ID and recorded Details; select Close when finished.
For document-specific evidence, also inspect its Approval History, Related Requests, or Transfer History.
slide_notes: The audit page is a read-only inspection screen; it does not provide an edit or delete operation for audit events.

sections.title: 22. Back up, import, and restore system data
steps: Open Backup & Restore. Read the backup status and Last automatic backup when shown. The page states a daily schedule of 5:00 PM, Asia/Manila.
To create a manual backup, select Backup now and confirm Create an encrypted backup of the current system. Check the archive list after completion.
Use the archive list's search and type filter to find Manual, Automatic, or Recovery backups. Select the available Download action when you need a copy.
To add an existing system backup, select Import backup, choose the Backup ZIP, submit Import backup, and confirm the verification and storage action.
To restore, select Restore system data, choose Backup to restore, enter Your password, and type RESTORE in Type RESTORE to confirm.
Read the replacement warning, select Restore selected backup, and confirm only after checking that the selected archive is the intended recovery point.
To remove old backup and log archives, select Clean up and confirm the removal of archives older than three months.
notes: Restore replaces live records and private files; the interface states that a recovery backup is created first. Perform it only as an authorized administrator following the organization's recovery procedure.
Backup actions require edit permission and may be disabled when backup configuration or readiness checks are not satisfied.
The displayed schedule and last-backup information do not by themselves prove that a future scheduled run has completed. Check the resulting archive and recorded time.
slide_steps: Open Backup & Restore; check readiness, the stated schedule, and Last automatic backup.
Select Backup now → Confirm to create an encrypted manual backup; inspect or download the resulting archive.
Use Import backup, choose Backup ZIP, then Import backup → Confirm to verify and store an existing archive.
To restore, select Restore system data, choose Backup to restore, enter Your password, and type RESTORE; then Restore selected backup → Confirm.
Use Clean up → Confirm to remove backup and log archives older than three months.
slide_notes: Restore replaces live records and private files; the interface states that a recovery backup is created first. Perform it only as an authorized administrator following the organization's recovery procedure.
